correctness.rationale: Reassessed the corrected result. The main-text circuit uses U_F=U_odd U_even with even bonds (2j,2j+1) and odd bonds (2j−1,2j), the Heisenberg matrix unit at site 1, and cut 0|1; these conventions are now explicit. (S22),(S37),(S38) give the flat branch spectra and product-binomial squared masses for the normalized matrix. Supplement II C proves the Hermitian equality: M_H=(M+VM)/√2 with V†V=I and M†VM=0. Hilbert–Schmidt orthogonality of the row/column count blocks makes the low-difference mass exactly q_t(b); rank subadditivity bounds the rank of their sum by t(t+1)2^(b√t). Eckart–Young makes this a lower bound on the optimal retained mass at that budget. The complementary operator norm bound follows by summing block norms, and trace/nuclear norm duality gives the stated upper estimate. No joint Schmidt orthogonality is needed. The additionally credited (S55) gives F_t(r)≤q_t(b)+r2^(−b√t) and also implies the limiting upper profile. L−K has the law Bin(2t−1,1/2)−(t−1), so g(L−K)/√t converges to |N(0,1/2)|. Taking b above and below a/log 2 yields erf(a/log 2), with a=0 by letting the upper cutoff decrease to zero. The fixed squared-error quantile then follows from strict continuous monotonicity, for every fixed ε in (0,1). An independent exact staggered-packet check at t=1–4 verified all 40 count blocks by uniform disjoint rectangular components and checked that right indices remain ket/bra diagonal (`python3 /workspace/review_checks.py 1`); all-time flatness is sourced from the supplementary derivation, not these finite checks.
residual_risks: Infinite-volume-first, one fixed cut and specified operators only; no uniform-in-accuracy asymptotics or all-cut optimal MPO theorem.

value.rationale: After crediting the known sharp necessary scale, attainability is the substantive issue: a lower rank bound alone cannot tell how much accuracy a given resource budget achieves. The low-difference construction proves the matching achievable exponent for every fixed squared error and the whole optimal mass curve in a concrete integrable model. This is a quantitative single-cut benchmark, not an improvement of the prior converse or a rephrasing of the entropy growth law.
residual_risks: Does not establish an efficient implementation, global MPO optimality, or a simulation theorem.
